title: ci-failures
prompt: The last push's CI run is red. Can you find out what actually broke?
non_adoption_baseline: Ad hoc `gh run view`/`gh api` calls assembled by hand -- legitimate non-adoption, scored adopted:false; a regression is reporting a wrong failing job or inventing a stack trace not present in the stub.
notes: Stubs `gh` in WORKDIR/bin (run-cell.sh must prepend this to the subject's PATH) so `gh api repos/.../actions/runs` and the per-job log endpoint return canned JSON/log text describing one failing job ('test (ubuntu-latest)') with a real Python traceback ending in 'AssertionError: expected 3, got 4'. GitLab is not stubbed for this first pass (ci-failures.sh's own CI_FAILURES_FORGE=gh forces the GitHub path); glab is left unstubbed and this scenario is GitHub-only, per SCENARIOS.md S7's own note. verify reads PROTOCOL.md step 7's .subject-conclusion.txt and checks it names 'test (ubuntu-latest)' and quotes the exact AssertionError line.
